newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill eight at Iranian centre in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill eight at Iranian centre in Pakistan.

text.p: Gunmen attacked an Iranian cultural centre in Pakistan's central province of Punjab on Thursday, killing eight people, including its Iranian director, government officials said.
They said several unidentified gunmen had forced their way into the cultural centre in Multan city, in southern Punjab, at around 1 p.m. (0800 GMT) and started shooting indiscriminately.
A government statement said that, apart from the centre's director Muhammad Ali Rahimi, the seven other people killed were Pakistanis, including a policeman and a civilian guard.
Earlier, police had put the number of dead at seven in this second attack on an Iranian cultural centre in Pakistan in a little over a month.
A statement issued by the Iranian consulate-general in the Punjab capital Lahore blamed unspecified "anti-Islamic agents of world imperialism" for Thursday's attack.
Punjab police chief Mohammad Amin said some people had been arrested but he would not disclose their identity at this stage.

On January 19, a crowd of militants from the Sunni Moslem sect ransacked and burned the Iranian cultural centre in Lahore a day after a bomb blast there killed Zia-ur-Rahman Faruqi, leader of the militant Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group.
SSP followers blamed mil government to protect Shi'ites from attacks by what it calls terrorists.
